description: A change that applies to exactly one base repository, carried as a patch, a git bundle, or a complete result tree, with the resulting git object ids recomputed by the platform rather than trusted.

body/repository_id.label: Repository
body/repository_id.description: A snapshot digest, which satisfies the identifier charset. Read out of the base repository and compared, so the producer transcribes it rather than choosing it.

body/base_sha.label: Base commit
body/base_sha.description: A full git object id. Its width selects the object format for every other object id in this record.

body/payload.label: Payload
body/payload.description: Where inside this sealed tree the change bytes live. The path is the producer's choice; the digest is recomputed over the exact bytes.

body/result_commit.label: Result commit
body/result_commit.description: Optional in the declared sense only: forbidden for a patch, which proves only a tree, and required for git-tree and git-bundle.

go_only_rules.rule: The repository id must parse as a snapshot digest: sha256 followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
The repository id must equal the id read out of the bound base repository.
The base commit must be a full 40-character sha1 or 64-character sha256 object id; its width selects the object format.
The base commit must equal the HEAD of the bound base repository.
The result tree and, when present, the result commit must be valid object ids in the same object format as the base repository.
A patch must omit the result commit, because a patch proves only the result tree; git-tree and git-bundle require it.
The payload path must resolve to a regular file inside this sealed tree, beneath content/, no larger than 10 GiB.
The payload digest is recomputed over the exact bytes at the payload path and any mismatch is rejected.
The result tree is recomputed — git write-tree after applying a patch in a controlled scratch repository, or the result repository's own tree for git-tree and git-bundle — and must match.
For git-tree and git-bundle the result commit must descend from the base commit, and a bundle must expose exactly one head equal to the result commit.

The change must actually apply or verify against the bound base repository: git apply --check --index for a patch, git bundle verify and unbundle for a bundle, a canonical repository tar for git-tree.
The changed file list is derived by the platform into intrinsic metadata and deliberately has no place in the record body, because server-derived data stays out of sealed bodies.
